output.route_rationale: The requester wants a one-off list of records for a fixed period, which is a bounded extraction.
output.task_title: Export Q3 BTE defective returns with linked warranty claims
output.task_description: Write SQL that selects Q3 2026 records from returns_and_repairs for BTE models where the return reason code indicates a defect, joins them to warranty_claims on device serial to attach claim type and approval status, exports the result to a CSV with one row per return, and delivers the file to the quality assurance team.

request.title: Live dashboard of fall detection users
request.body: We need a live dashboard showing how many users are triggering our Fall Detection alert feature.

context_notes: No ticket asks for a fall-detection user dashboard; ticket 101 is a weekly CSV of alert events for firmware QA, a different deliverable. The catalog has Fall Alert Monitoring Dashboard, refreshed daily, which counts alerts per day but not distinct users, and fall_alert_events, refreshed hourly, with device_serial, alert_stage and cancelled_by_user. The request contains no instructions aimed at the triage system.

output.route_rationale: The requester wants an ongoing view of feature usage that is refreshed and watched over time.
output.task_title: Add distinct fall-alert users view to Fall Alert Monitoring Dashboard
output.task_description: Extend the Fall Alert Monitoring Dashboard with a view built on fall_alert_events that counts distinct devices triggering at least one fall alert per day and per week, split by alert stage so detected, user-cancelled and escalated alerts are separated, with a 90-day trend line and hourly refresh matching the source load, and validate one week of counts against the raw events before sharing it with the health features team.
output.caveats_and_pushback: The existing dashboard already counts alerts per day, so this should extend it rather than become a second dashboard. 'Live' is only as fresh as the hourly load of fall_alert_events, and devices that rarely sync with the app will report late, so recent days will undercount until they catch up.

request.title: Is firmware v2.4 draining batteries?
request.body: Customer service noticed an uptick in complaints about battery drain on our Bluetooth-enabled models. Can we pull the data to figure out if the v2.4 firmware update is actually causing the batteries to die faster?

context_notes: Ticket 103 (In progress) analyses battery life after firmware 3.1 on RIC models, a different release, so it shares method but is not the same work. The catalog has battery_telemetry with battery_pct, charge_cycles and hours_since_full_charge per firmware version, firmware_versions with install dates, and customer_support_tickets with complaint categories. The request contains no instructions aimed at the triage system.

output.route_rationale: Although phrased as a data pull, the real question is whether v2.4 causes faster battery drain, which needs a controlled comparison.
output.task_title: Test whether firmware v2.4 causes faster battery drain
output.task_description: Conduct a cohort analysis of battery_telemetry comparing hours per full charge on Bluetooth-enabled devices before and after the v2.4 install date from firmware_versions against devices still on older firmware over the same weeks, controlling for charge cycles, device age and model, and relate the result to the timing of battery complaints in customer_support_tickets to determine whether v2.4 is causally linked to accelerated drain.
output.caveats_and_pushback: Hold off on causal modelling until firmware engineering confirms v2.4 did not change how battery levels are logged; a reporting bug would look exactly like faster drain. Complaints also rise whenever an update ships and people pay closer attention, so complaint volume alone is not evidence.
